facts.text: Don Larsen of the New York Yankees threw a perfect game in Game 5 of the 1956 World Series on October 8, 1956, beating the Brooklyn Dodgers 2-0 with Yogi Berra catching. It remains the only perfect game in World Series history; he struck out seven and was named Series MVP.

Roy Halladay of the Phillies threw a no-hitter against the Cincinnati Reds in Game 1 of the 2010 NLDS on October 6, 2010 (4-0), and is the only pitcher with no-hitters in both the regular season (his May 29, 2010 perfect game) and postseason.

Bill Mazeroski hit a ninth-inning home run in Game 7 of the 1960 World Series to give the Pittsburgh Pirates the title over the Yankees; it was the first World Series to end on a home run and the first winner-take-all World Series game to end that way.

The 1960 Yankees outscored the Pirates but lost: they scored 55 runs, the most by any team in a World Series, yet Pittsburgh won 4-3. Bobby Richardson was MVP, the first non-pitcher MVP and the only MVP from a losing team.

Carlton Fisk's walk-off home run won Game 6 of the 1975 World Series for the Red Sox in the 12th inning (7-6 over the Reds) at Fenway Park; the Reds then won Game 7 on a ninth-inning Joe Morgan single.

Kirk Gibson, injured in both legs and not starting, hit a pinch-hit walk-off home run off Oakland closer Dennis Eckersley in Game 1 of the 1988 World Series; the Dodgers won in five games and Orel Hershiser was MVP.
Orel Hershiser set the all-time scoreless-inning streak at 59 innings in the 1988 regular season, then won the Series MVP.

Joe Carter hit a walk-off three-run home run in the bottom of the ninth of Game 6 of the 1993 World Series, with Toronto trailing the Phillies 6-5, to clinch the Blue Jays' second straight title. It was only the second World Series ended by a home run (after Mazeroski in 1960).

In Game 6 of the 1986 World Series the Mets rallied with two outs and nobody on in the bottom of the 10th, won on an error by Red Sox first baseman Bill Buckner, with Boston twice one strike from the title; the Mets then won Game 7. The collapse became part of the Curse of the Bambino lore.

David Freese hit a game-tying two-run triple in the ninth and a walk-off home run in the 11th of Game 6 of the 2011 World Series (Cardinals 10, Rangers 9); St. Louis twice came back from two runs down, each time with Texas one strike from a title. Freese was Series MVP and the Cardinals won in seven.
Albert Pujols hit three home runs in Game 3 of the 2011 World Series, a feat previously done only by Reggie Jackson and Babe Ruth and later by Pablo Sandoval in 2012.

Game 3 of the 2018 World Series lasted 18 innings and 7 hours 20 minutes, the longest World Series game by innings and time: Max Muncy homered in the bottom of the 18th to give the Dodgers a 3-2 win over the Red Sox (October 26, 2018). The Red Sox still won the Series 4-1.

Game 3 of the 2025 World Series also went 18 innings: Freddie Freeman hit a walk-off home run off Brendon Little in the 18th for the Dodgers over the Blue Jays; it was the second-longest World Series game by time.

The 2025 World Series: the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Toronto Blue Jays 4-3, winning Game 7 in 11 innings (Miguel Rojas tied it with a two-out ninth-inning homer, Will Smith hit the go-ahead homer in the 11th). Yoshinobu Yamamoto was Series MVP. Dodgers were the first back-to-back champion since the 2000 Yankees.

Reggie Jackson hit three consecutive home runs in the clinching Game 6 of the 1977 World Series at Yankee Stadium (five home runs in the Series) and was MVP; this is the root of his 'Mr. October' nickname.

The Chicago Cubs won the 2016 World Series 4-3 over Cleveland, winning Game 7 8-7 in ten innings after a rain delay and coming back from a 3-1 deficit; it was their first title since 1908 and ended what Wikipedia calls the longest championship drought in North American pro sports history.

The Curse of the Bambino was the superstition behind the Red Sox's 86-year drought (1918-2004), tied to Harry Frazee selling Babe Ruth to the Yankees; it ended with a 4-0 sweep of the Cardinals in 2004 after beating the Yankees in the ALCS following a 0-3 deficit.
The Curse of the Billy Goat on the Cubs dated to Game 4 of the 1945 World Series at Wrigley Field, when tavern owner William Sianis and his goat Murphy were ejected; it lasted 71 years until 2016.
The Texas Rangers' 2011 World Series Game 6 collapse was blamed by some fans on the 'Curse of Bob Short'; they won their first title in 2023 under Bruce Bochy over Arizona, 4-1.

The Black Sox Scandal: eight Chicago White Sox players were accused of intentionally losing the 1919 World Series to the Cincinnati Reds (won 5-3 in best-of-nine); Commissioner Kenesaw Mountain Landis banned all eight for life despite their 1921 acquittal.
The 1904 World Series was never played: with no governing body, New York Giants owner John T. Brush refused to play the AL champion Boston Americans.
The first World Series (1903) was a best-of-nine won by the Boston Americans (later Red Sox) over the Pittsburgh Pirates, 5-3; the best-of-nine format was also used 1919-1921.

Postseason format history: League Championship Series added in 1969 with divisions; wild card and Division Series introduced for 1994, first played in 1995 (the 1994 postseason was cancelled by a strike); a one-game Wild Card playoff and second wild card added in 2012; a temporary 16-team format in 2020; the 12-team format (6 per league, best-of-three Wild Card Series) since 2022.
The 1994 World Series was cancelled because of the players' strike; it is one of only two years (with 1904) in which no World Series was played since 1903.

Randy Arozarena of the 2020 Rays hit a record 10 home runs in a single postseason (with single-postseason records for hits, 29, and total bases). Next with 8: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Shohei Ohtani (2025), Barry Bonds (2002), Carlos Beltran (2004), Nelson Cruz (2011), Corey Seager (2020), Adolis Garcia (2023).
Nelson Cruz hit six home runs in the 2011 ALCS, the most by a player in any single postseason series; Jose Altuve hit three homers in Game 1 of the 2017 ALDS.

Career postseason home run leaders per Wikipedia's records list: Manny Ramirez 29, Jose Altuve 28 (a 2026 MLB.com article says Altuve was one behind Ramirez after a 2026 Wild Card Series homer, so totals are still moving this October), Kyle Schwarber 24, George Springer 23, Bernie Williams 22, Derek Jeter 20.
Altuve hit a record eight first-inning postseason home runs and hit the pennant-clinching walk-off home run off Aroldis Chapman in Game 6 of the 2019 ALCS.

Postseason career records (Wikipedia list): Derek Jeter leads in hits (200) and, among batters, in strikeouts (135); Justin Verlander leads pitchers in postseason strikeouts (244), ahead of Clayton Kershaw (213) and John Smoltz (199).

There have been 19 World Series sweeps; the first was by the 1914 Boston Braves over the Philadelphia Athletics, the Yankees hold a record eight, and the most recent (as listed) was the 2012 Giants over the Tigers. The Yankees swept in 1998 and 1999.

Game 7 of the 1991 World Series was a 1-0 Twins win in 10 innings over the Braves, with Jack Morris pitching a complete-game shutout (MVP); the series is called the 'Greatest of All Time' by ESPN. Kirby Puckett hit a walk-off homer in Game 6.

Game 7 of the 1997 World Series ended on a Craig Counsell walk-off hit as the Florida Marlins (in their fifth season) beat the Indians; the 2016 Game 7 was the fifth World Series Game 7 to go to extra innings and the 2025 Game 7 was the sixth.

The 1921 World Series was the first Subway Series (Giants vs Yankees, first meeting October 5, 1921); the Yankees' 2000 World Series win over the Mets was a Subway Series, and Subway Series have also involved the Brooklyn Dodgers (the Dodgers lost to the Yankees in 1941, 1947, 1949, 1952, 1953, 1956 and beat them in 1955).
Brooklyn Dodgers won their only Brooklyn World Series in 1955 over the Yankees in seven games; MVP Johnny Podres, the first World Series MVP.

Only franchise from outside the US to win a World Series is the Toronto Blue Jays (1992, 1993); the Houston Astros are the only team to represent both leagues in a World Series (NL 2005, AL 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022).
The 2017 and 1919 World Series were both marred by cheating scandals (Astros sign stealing in 2017).

The 2001 World Series ended in a Game 7 walk-off bases-loaded blooper off Mariano Rivera as the Diamondbacks beat the Yankees 4-3; Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling shared MVP and combined for all four Arizona wins.
The 2019 World Series: the Washington Nationals beat the Houston Astros 4-3, winning all four road games; Stephen Strasburg MVP; the Nationals' first title.

Jose Altuve (7 HR, 2017), Daniel Murphy (2015, homers in six straight postseason games), B.J. Upton (2008), Jayson Werth (2009), Troy Glaus (2002) and Giancarlo Stanton (2024, Yankees record) each hit 7 homers in a postseason.

Corey Seager is a two-time World Series MVP with different teams (2020 Dodgers, 2023 Rangers); Freddie Freeman (2024) hit a walk-off grand slam in Game 1 of the 2024 World Series and a walk-off homer in Game 3 of 2025.
